text:
li: FYI canary p99 jumped after kernel switch on g4x-pool.
li: saw ~2.2x p99 latency vs baseline.
sam: which kernel? the aten->cuopt_agg one?
li: yup. profiler shows worse SM utilization and stalls on matmul.
li: kv-cache miss rate also spiked from 0.6% to 6.8% (canary logs).
nisha: did microbatch size change in rollout config?
eric: we changed microbatch from 4 -> 8 to increase throughput in canary.
li: here's quick metrics dump:
```
canary_id=pr-4578    model=redwood-2
baseline: p95=42ms p99=88ms GPU_util=72% kv_miss=0.6%
canary:   p95=44ms p99=193ms GPU_util=95% kv_miss=6.8%
``` 
sam: 95% util + higher kv_miss => tail spikes from preemption/long kernels.
nisha: that combination means less headroom for bursts, queueing increases p99.
eric: ops, please hold canary and rollback kernel flag for pr-4578. @deploy-bot can you revert?
deploy-bot: received. initiating rollback of kernel flag in canary pool :hourglass: 
li: also propose short-term mitigations: force microbatch=4 for that pool, disable kernel auto-switch for seq_len>1024, and add admission soft-drop at queue_length>8.
nisha: run sim of soft-drop at 10% shed vs 20% shed? I can run ct-sim.
sam: quick sim results: 10% shed -> p99 120ms, throughput -6%; 20% shed -> p99 95ms, throughput -14%.
li: sounds like 10% may be best immediate tradeoff. Also add kv-prefetch warmup for suspected long contexts.
eric: create followup infra ticket with perf traces and revert timeline.
li: created https://go/infra/RED-1234 with CPU/GPU traces and the profiler outputs.
nisha: I'll run deeper kernel perf analysis tomorrow, focusing on sgemm tiling and l2 thrash.
sam: thanks all. keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
